title: Event listener options and cleanup
learningObjectives: Explain event listener options and cleanup and implement reliable browser event and network workflows.

understand.concept: addEventListener accepts capture, once, passive, and signal options. once removes a listener after its first call; passive indicates it will not cancel the default action; signal links listener lifetime to an AbortController.
understand.whyItMatters: Explicit options simplify listener lifecycle and avoid unnecessary work. Remove listeners when a component is no longer active.
understand.analogy: Listener options define when a listener runs and how long it remains registered.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scheduling, HTTP semantics, and browser security follow platform standards.

explain.narrative: The listener is configured to run once and can also be removed early by aborting the signal.

examples.explanation: The listener is configured to run once and can also be removed early by aborting the signal.
examples.expectedOutput: Console or UI output demonstrates the concept; network examples require a configured endpoint.

practise.guidedTask: Create a group of listeners with one AbortController and abort them when a view is removed.
practise.independentTask: Build an asynchronous feature with explicit states, cancellation, and error handling. Document which failures are safe to retry.
hints: Separate HTTP errors from network and parsing errors.
Use bounded retries only for suitable operations.
Tie UI updates to the latest active request.

questions.prompt: Which option removes a listener after its first invocation?
questions.explanation: The once option automatically removes the listener after it runs once.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach to network-driven UI?
options: Model loading, empty, success, failure, and cancellation states
Assume every fulfilled fetch means HTTP success
questions.answer: Model loading, empty, success, failure, and cancellation states
questions.explanation: Explicit states and bounded recovery make network interfaces predictable and safe.
